source: Quiz 4 - Sessions 1-5: Building and Improving Agent Skills
question: Why can two skills with vague, overlapping descriptions lead to poor selection?

options.text: Their descriptions fail to distinguish the intended uses
options.feedback: Selection begins with compact guidance about relevance. Similar vague descriptions can make different procedures appear interchangeable.

options.text: Their latest modification dates determine which procedure fits
options.feedback: Modification dates do not establish task fit. Clear differences in purpose and applicability are more useful selection evidence.

options.text: Their overlapping words prove the procedures are interchangeable
options.feedback: Similar wording can hide different procedures. The overlap creates ambiguity rather than proving the skills do the same work.

options.text: Their shared vocabulary makes the full instructions unnecessary
options.feedback: A description supports initial selection. Overlapping vocabulary does not replace the detailed instructions for carrying out the work.
